introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO questions from Section C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Draw a fairly large annotated sketch of the portion east of Longitude 9°25' and north of latitude 4°40' and insert the following features:

- The Cardbury and Fry plantation *(2 marks)*
- The tarred road east of the plantation *(2 marks)*
- Shade the area covered by forest vegetation *(2 marks)*
- Add a key and an appropriate title *(1 mark)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**What the examiner wants.** A sketch map, not a copy: simple, neat, in pencil, with only the features asked for, a frame, a key and a title.

**Step 1 - Find the portion on the map.** The vertical grid line marked 9°25' and the horizontal line marked 4°40' cross close to Lake Barombi Mbo. The required portion is the block *to the east* of the first line and *to the north* of the second: the north-eastern part of the extract, bounded on the east by the 9°30' edge and on the north by the 4°45' edge. It is a block of 5 minutes by 5 minutes, which at this latitude is roughly 9 km by 9 km (about 18 cm square on the 1:50,000 map).

**Step 2 - Draw the frame.** Draw a square frame, for example 9 cm by 9 cm (the sketch is therefore at about 1:100,000, one centimetre for one kilometre). Label the corners 9°25'E, 9°30'E, 4°40'N and 4°45'N. Add a north arrow.

**Step 3 - Insert the features** (see the model sketch below).
- *Cardbury (Cadbury) and Fry plantation:* in the north-east part, a dotted (plantation symbol) block, roughly 2.5 km across, around the labels Ikiliwindi I (Mile 10) and the plantation name; draw its outline and label it.
- *Tarred road east of the plantation:* the double-line (asphalted) road enters at the top edge (it is signed to Mamfe), swings east around Ikiliwindi II, then runs southwards along the eastern edge of the plantation and leaves the portion near the 4°40' line towards Kumba. Draw it as a thick double or solid line and label it.
- *Forest vegetation:* the dark green area covers most of the block (north, centre and west). Shade it (colour or close hatching) and leave the clearings (the plantation, the cleared patches near Motor Butu and along the road, and the small clearing south-west of the plantation) unshaded.
- *Key and title:* a boxed key with one line for each symbol (forest, cleared land, plantation, tarred road) and a title such as "Sketch map of the area east of 9°25'E and north of 4°40'N, Kumba".

![fig-3](gce-al-geography-2020-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

**Marking guide.** Plantation correctly placed and labelled 2; tarred road correctly placed east of the plantation 2; forest shading 2; key and title 1. Marks are lost for copying contours and every detail, a missing frame or a title that is not specific.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Describe the relief characteristics of the area east of Longitude 9°25' and south of Latitude 4°40'. *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Area concerned.** The south-eastern quarter of the extract, which contains the town of Kumba, the junction at Mambanda and the lower part of the tarred road.

**Description (4 well-made points).**
1. *Altitude:* a low-lying area. The spot heights and bench marks are of the order of 190 to 230 m above sea level (for example values around 193, 207, 210 and 221 m are shown), so there are no high summits in this block.
2. *Slope:* the contours are generally widely spaced, which means gentle slopes and a gently undulating to almost flat surface. Steeper ground, shown by closer contours, is limited to a few small rises.
3. *Landforms:* low rounded hills and small isolated knolls with concentric contours (for example the small rise east of the junction at Mambanda) alternate with shallow valleys; the broad ridge on which Kumba lies is only slightly higher than the surrounding ground.
4. *General trend:* the land rises gradually northwards and westwards towards the forested uplands and the crater rim of Lake Barombi Mbo, and falls gently south-eastwards; stream valleys are shallow and the lower ground near some streams is marshy.

**Examiner's remark.** Always quote map evidence (spot heights, contour spacing) and give the direction of the slope. A pure list of words (gentle, hilly) without evidence earns only half marks.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) What evidence from the map suggests that Lake Barombi Mbo is a crater lake? *(3 marks)*

(ii) Comment on the distribution of vegetation on the map. *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Evidence that Lake Barombi Mbo is a crater lake (3 marks).**
- *Shape:* the lake is almost circular, about 2 km across, which is typical of an explosion crater (a maar) and unlike a lake formed in a river valley, which is elongated and follows the valley.
- *Relief around it:* it lies in a basin enclosed by closely spaced contours on all sides, i.e. steep inner walls, with a raised rim whose spot heights (several hundred metres, values around 300 to 450 m appear on and around the rim) are well above the surrounding lowlands to the south (about 200 m).
- *Drainage:* no large river enters or leaves the lake (at most a small stream drains from its south-eastern corner); the water is held in a closed depression, as is usual in a crater.
- *Setting:* it lies in the volcanic zone of the Cameroon line and is protected as a forest reserve (the words Forest Reserve are printed around the lake). Any three well explained points earn full marks.

**(ii) Distribution of vegetation (4 marks).**
- *Dense (secondary) forest* in dark green covers the greater part of the extract: the whole north, the centre and the west, including the slopes around Lake Barombi Mbo (a protected forest reserve).
- *Clearings* with scattered trees or cultivation appear as white patches with dots within the forest, mainly around Motor Butu in the north, along the road in the west and around the plantation and the settlements of Ikiliwindi in the north-east.
- *Plantation* (dotted pattern) is concentrated in the north-east on the cleared land along the tarred road; the small speckled patch east of the lake is a thicket or wooded savanna.
- *South and south-east:* around Kumba the forest has been replaced by built-up land, farmland and scattered trees, so vegetation becomes sparse and cultivated.
- *Explanation:* the forest survives where the relief is hilly, the land is protected (forest reserve) and access is difficult; it has been cleared where there are roads, settlements and level land.

**Marking guide.** 1 mark for each evidence point in (i); in (ii) 1 mark for each of the four distribution/explanation points.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Explain with evidence from the map why you think Kumba is a fairly well planned cosmopolitan settlement? *(3 marks)*

(ii) Calculate the Detour Index (D.I) of the road from the Mabanda junction in the South East to the end point of the road North of Ikiliwindi. *(3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) A fairly well planned cosmopolitan settlement (3 marks).**
- *Planned layout:* the roads of the built-up area form a fairly regular pattern, with a grid in the new quarters and routes that converge on the centre, instead of random lanes.
- *Functional zones:* the built-up area is divided into distinct quarters (a commercial/administrative core and residential quarters, each with its own name, for example Buea Road Quarter), and the town has all-weather tarred roads, junctions (for example Three Corners) and services such as schools, churches, mosques, a market and health facilities as given in the key.
- *Cosmopolitan:* the quarters named after different peoples or places of origin, and the presence of both churches and mosques, show that people of many ethnic and religious backgrounds live together; the size of the built-up area shows a large and diverse population attracted by trade, plantations and administration.

**(ii) Detour Index (3 marks).**

*Definition.* The Detour Index measures how direct a route is:

$$
\text{D.I.} = \frac{\text{actual distance along the road}}{\text{straight-line distance between the two end points}}
$$

(some textbooks multiply by 100 and give a percentage).

*Method.*
1. Locate the junction at Mambanda in the south-east and the northern end of the tarred road (north of Ikiliwindi II, signed to Mamfe).
2. Lay a thread along every bend of the road between the two points; straighten it and measure it against the scale line: actual distance.
3. Measure the straight line between the two points with a ruler: straight-line distance.
4. Convert with the scale 1:50,000 (1 cm = 0.5 km) and divide.

*Reading from the extract (approximate, the scan is of poor quality).* Road length along the thread about 25.2 cm, that is $25.2 \times 0.5 = 12.6$ km; straight line about 24.0 cm, that is $24.0 \times 0.5 = 12.0$ km.

$$
\text{D.I.} = \frac{12.6}{12.0} = 1.05
$$

*Conclusion.* The D.I. is only slightly above 1 (about 1.05, or 105 per cent): the road is almost straight and direct, because the relief along its route is gentle and the road was built to link Kumba with Mamfe. Any answer close to 1.0 to 1.1 with a clear method is accepted.

questions.enonce_markdown: (e) Account for the restriction of the road network to the south of the map area. *(3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Fact to explain.** Almost all the roads and streets are in the south, around Kumba; the north and west have only the one long tarred road, a few jeep tracks (for logging) and some footpaths.

**Reasons (any three well developed).**
1. *Dense forest and forest reserve:* the north and west are covered by thick forest, much of it protected, so roads would be costly to cut and maintain, and the law limits clearing.
2. *Relief:* the northern and western parts are hilly and, around Lake Barombi Mbo, have a steep crater rim and a lake basin, which makes road building difficult and expensive (cuttings, bridges, drainage).
3. *Low population and few economic activities:* there are few settlements and little demand for roads outside the plantation and the timber camps, whereas the south has the town, its markets, services and farmland.
4. *Town as a focus:* Kumba is a route centre and its trade and administration generate many streets and roads that radiate from the centre.
5. *Gentle relief and cleared land in the south* make road building cheap.

questions.enonce_markdown: (f) Why are settlements mostly concentrated in the south of the map area? *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Observation.** Almost all the built-up land (Kumba, Mambanda, Three Corners and many villages) lies in the south, while the north has only a few small settlements, camps and plantation villages (Ikiliwindi I and II).

**Explanation (four points, each with evidence).**
1. *Relief:* the south is low and gently sloping (spot heights of about 190 to 230 m), with room for building; the north and west are hilly and forested.
2. *Accessibility:* the main tarred road and the road junctions (Mambanda, Three Corners) are in the south, so people settle along them for transport and trade.
3. *Economic opportunities:* Kumba is a market and service town (administration, schools, health, trade), which attracts migrants and creates jobs; farmland, small plantations and fertile volcanic soils are close by.
4. *Land and security of tenure:* the forest in the north and around the lake is a protected reserve, so settlement is forbidden or discouraged, and the dense forest is hostile (disease, wild animals, isolation); the lake basin has steep slopes.
5. *Water supply:* streams and springs in the south supply water for domestic use and farming.

**Marking guide.** 1 mark for each valid factor explained with map evidence, maximum 4.
